title: Pollution types
examples: What is the difference between air and water pollution?
Can you give me an example of light pollution?
What are some common sources of land pollution?

explain.say: Today we are learning about different types of pollution. Pollution means making something dirty or harmful. We will look at five main types today.

draw.text: Pollution Types: Air, Water, Land, Noise, Light

explain.say: Air pollution happens when the air becomes dirty. A common source is car exhaust fumes. These fumes contain harmful gases we breathe.
Water pollution is when water bodies get contaminated. Sewage and industrial waste are major sources of this pollution. This harms fish and other aquatic life.
Land pollution means the ground becomes contaminated. Dumping rubbish and chemicals are key sources of this problem. This affects soil health for plants.
Noise pollution is unwanted or excessive sound. Loud construction sites and traffic are common sources. This can disturb wildlife and people's peace.
Light pollution is excessive artificial outdoor lighting. Unshielded streetlights and building signs are main sources. This affects nocturnal animals like insects.

faq.q: What is the biggest source of air pollution?
faq.a: The biggest sources often include vehicle emissions and industrial burning of fossil fuels. You might also ask about smog or burning trash.
asks: Where does bad air come from?

faq.q: How does sewage cause water pollution?
faq.a: Sewage introduces harmful bacteria and nutrients into rivers and lakes. Another way to ask is what makes water unsafe for drinking.
asks: What is the impact of raw sewage?

faq.q: Is plastic waste the only cause of land pollution?
faq.a: No, chemical spills and improper disposal of batteries are also major contributors. You could also ask about landfill size.

faq.q: Does noise pollution only affect animals?
faq.a: No, it can also cause stress and hearing issues in humans. You might ask about quiet zones in cities.
asks: Can people get sick from loud noises?

faq.q: Why is light pollution bad for nature?
faq.a: It confuses animals that use natural light cycles, like migrating birds or sea turtles. Another way is to ask about starry nights.
asks: Why should we cover our lights?

facts: Air pollution can contain harmful gases like carbon monoxide.
Water pollution can reduce the oxygen levels in rivers.
Land pollution often involves the buildup of non-biodegradable waste.
Noise pollution is measured in units called decibels.
Light pollution disrupts the natural cycles of nocturnal wildlife.

quiz.say: Which pollution type is caused by exhaust fumes from cars?
quiz.why: Car exhaust fumes are a primary source of airborne pollutants.

wrong.0: Water pollution relates to liquids, not gases from engines.
wrong.1: Land pollution involves solid waste on the ground surface.
wrong.2: Noise pollution is about unwanted sound levels.

quiz.say: If a river is filled with oil and sewage, what type of pollution is present?
quiz.why: Oil and sewage are contaminants found in water bodies.

wrong.1: While waste can reach land, the primary medium here is water.
wrong.2: Air pollution involves gases and smoke in the atmosphere.
wrong.3: Light pollution relates to excessive artificial illumination.

quiz.say: Which pollution type is best reduced by using downward-facing, shielded outdoor lights?
quiz.why: Shielding lights prevents excessive upward and sideways glow, reducing light pollution.

wrong.0: Water pollution needs filtration or waste treatment systems.
wrong.2: Noise reduction uses sound barriers or quiet zones.
wrong.3: Air pollution is controlled by filtering emissions, not light shields.
